title: Should attendance be mandatory in Indian colleges?
description: The debate examines whether Indian colleges should require minimum classroom attendance for academic eligibility and learning.

facts.fact: UGC's 2003 first-degree regulations (clause 5.8) say required attendance should ordinarily be at least 75% of lectures, tutorials, seminars and practicals.
A 2010 meta-analysis of 69 studies (21,195 students) found class attendance strongly related to grades (ρ = 0.44) and GPA (ρ = 0.41).
The same 2010 meta-analysis found that mandatory attendance policies had a small positive effect on average grades (d = 0.21).
In November 2025 the Delhi High Court held that no law student can be barred from exams or promotion merely for shortage of attendance.
Delhi High Court later applied that precedent to DU students, ruling that attendance shortage alone has no legal basis for barring exams.
UGC's December 2024 draft regulations let institutions set their own minimum attendance, recognising online, hybrid and in-person learning.
